title: Optimal bounds for an Erdős problem on matching integers to distinct multiples
summary: Let $f(m)$ be the largest integer such that for every set $A = \{a_1 < \cdots < a_m\}$ of $m$ positive integers and every open interval $I$ of length $2a_m$, there exist at least $f(m)$ disjoint pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \in A$ dividing $b \in I$. Solving a problem of Erdős, we determine $f(m)$ exactly, and show $$ f(m)=\min\bigl(m,\lceil 2\sqrt{m}\,\rceil\bigr) $$ for all $m$. The proof was obtained through an AI-assisted workflow: the proof strategy was first proposed by ChatGPT, and the detailed argument was subsequently made fully rigorous and formally verified in Lean by Aristotle.
